The engraving is the only picture of the range's face

differences.what: the rear range's length: the print closes the range in a cornice return at x 125 px, about 8 m behind the main body through this camera, where the 1911 sheet's plan draws it 11.9 m (its far end at x 63, where the print draws a tree with sky above it)
differences.how: T-1886 (2026-11-15): the measured plan (the 1911 sheet) and the engraving disagree about the range's far 4 m, and the engraver's vignette closes on that tree; the sheet's plan is kept (T-3153: a gap two sources disagree about). The photograph, whose camera sees only that far end, is argued in its own record

differences.what: the range's lower storey and the lot line in front of it: a board fence (x 60-180, y 480-680 px) hides them
differences.how: T-1886 (2026-11-15): the print cannot say what the lower storey's openings were; the board fence is of 1874 and the 1904 boundary is built to the photograph and the sheet

differences.what: no raised crown over the street front's south end: the main mansard runs on unbroken from the corner to the north end, with three pedimented dormers evenly spaced in its street face (x 420-455, 485-520, 555-595 px)
differences.how: T-1886 (2026-11-15): the engraving is of May 1874, the year after the house was built, and cannot say what stood in 1904; the undated later photograph (chicagology_photo, after 1873) shows the front's canted bay carried up into a raised crown over that end, standing higher than the main roof, with its own dormer, and two dormers in the main street face beside it, so the crown is read as an alteration after 1874, and the 1904 scene is built to it; the three dormers' places are the 1874 roof's
